rationale: The configured generic extcon framework must not reuse a connector ID until device_unregister has removed its device name. The release callback in pinned LTS is empty and object storage has separate ownership, so moving ida_free afterward does not dereference freed extcon storage. This prevents registration collisions without changing LTS lifetime rules.

The SDK uses ext4 and enables Unicode/casefold support. Pinned LTS still invalidates a casefolded dentry while holding a journal handle; eviction of child dentries can wait on that transaction, causing a deadlock. Stop the transaction before d_invalidate and guard invalidation on successful removal. The cherry-pick preserves all other newer LTS namei fixes and closes an availability failure.

F2FS remains enabled for Android configuration compatibility. Pinned LTS has the inline-directory conversion bounds check but lacks this lookup check. Reject an on-disk name length above F2FS_NAME_LEN or extending past the available filename slots before comparing it. This prevents out-of-bounds reads from malformed directory entries; existing LTS error cleanup and inode validation are unchanged.

The configured block scheduler permits concurrent sysfs scheduler changes. Pinned LTS retains the two-stage elevator_change/elevator_change_done sequence and a shared read lock, which permits concurrent kobject cleanup and memory corruption. Use the writer trylock for the whole switch, retaining the LTS trylock/EBUSY behavior that avoids the kernfs disk-deletion lock cycle.

Associated KUnit sources are retained but were not executed or enabled by the SDK build; no runtime claim is made. The SDK enables BLK_INLINE_ENCRYPTION_FALLBACK and DM_DEFAULT_KEY; native LTS __submit_bio invokes crypto preparation while current->bio_list is active, so recursive encrypted submissions can hold the resources an allocation awaits. Adapt the ACK rescue-list/workqueue fix to native per-page LTS allocation: nonblocking bio/page allocation in recursive submission, enqueue remaining source with its updated DUN, and retry outside recursion. When a partially filled bounce bio exhausts pages, submit it with an extra source completion reference before continuing; only an empty worker bio may block. This avoids both recursive-submit deadlock and waiting on pages held by the current partial bio without importing the bulk-mempool refactor. Preserve early LTS alignment validation, on-stack requests, native completion/error behavior and dm-default-key skip-bit propagation. Availability/security rationale and compile-only verification limits are in SECURITY.md.
